tells: 1. The wide reads as a posed group photo, not a room: the whole front row sits square to camera with hands placed on the tables in near-identical rest poses, and nobody is drinking, leaning to a neighbour or slouching (club-1-wide.png, front row across the centre)

2. The laugh never builds. Over 1 s the only changes are small head turns and one hand rising in the white blouse; the pink-jacket man turns away from the stage and no mouths open wide or shoulders lift (club-5-strip.png, front row, all six frames)

3. The candles are not lighting anything. Faces carry a cool, even frontal key from above, with no warm under-fill from the tea-lights a metre away, so the practicals read as stickers rather than sources (club-2-mid.png and club-3-mid.png, table candles against the faces above them)

4. The face close shows low-poly faceting on the jaw, collar and shoulder, waxy skin with no subsurface, eyes cut sideways toward nothing, and a soft, out-of-focus hand blob at the bottom edge (club-4-face.png, centre face and bottom centre)

5. The back rows are flat dark cut-outs with no volume or rim, and the bright bar panel behind them looks like a pasted card. Depth falls off in steps, not as atmosphere (club-1-wide.png, upper-middle rows and the bar sign; also club-6-held.png, a stray hand on the green hoodie's shoulder at the right edge)

1. The front two rows are lit by a flat, unmotivated frontal flood: equal exposure on every body, no falloff from the stage edge and no shaping, so they look pasted over a black void. The rows behind them drop straight to pure silhouette (theatre-1-wide.png, centre block against the black upper half)

2. The back stalls are cardboard: black cut-out heads with hard rims and no seat or body detail, plus bright point lights sitting among them like stars (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-2-mid.png, upper third)

3. Stray flesh-coloured hand and arm fragments float beside the subject, with untextured, box-shaped red seats and faceted low-poly jackets in the close (theatre-4-face.png, left edge at mid-height, right edge near 1060,510, and the seat blocks at the bottom)

4. Postures are stiff and repeated: knees together, hands clasped between the thighs or on the knees in the same pose along the front row, and some bodies hover with no visible seat under them (theatre-1-wide.png front row; theatre-3-mid.png, left group of four)

5. The laugh in the strip is a scatter of open mouths at 12.6–12.8 s with no body follow-through. Heads barely move, and the dark-cap man's face stays hidden and his hair texture blotches (theatre-5-strip.png, front row; theatre-3-mid.png, bottom-right man)

1. The held frame and the wide are nearly identical: the same poses, the same lean and the same hand placement, so the room reads as frozen between beats (openmic-1-wide.png vs openmic-6-held.png, the whole front block)

2. The exposure is muddy and monochrome sepia: the faces in the wide sit near black with no key separating them from the wall, and the row of ceiling pin-spots lights nothing below it, so the light has no motivation (openmic-1-wide.png, centre and the ceiling lights)

3. In the face close, the hair edge breaks into a hard, dithered, noisy fringe (aliasing), and the blonde woman's hand behind is a smeared, ghosted mess (openmic-4-face.png, top right of the hair at about 780–880,80–330, and the hand at about 1150,600)
4. The whole front row hunches forward with hands on knees in the same lean, a synchronised, mannequin pose (openmic-1-wide.png and openmic-3-mid.png, the front row)

5. The red-jacket man in the second row has a bright patch over his mouth (a face artefact), the wall behind is a flat painted plane, and a lone green exit sign is the only cool accent (openmic-3-mid.png, at about 500,345, and the upper-left wall). The laugh build in the strip is the venue's one strength: the two women lean together, though the men beside them stay inert (openmic-5-strip.png)
